verdicts.rewritten_summary: April 2025 Washington Blade dateline Buenos Aires: the national framework this province falls under - the Feb 5, 2025 decree restricts minors' access to gender-affirming surgeries and hormone treatment; trans people hired under the 1% Trans Labor Quota were dismissed and the federal anti-discrimination agency INADI abolished; activists report police violence against trans and travesti sex workers has worsened since Milei took office and is worst outside Buenos Aires, in the more conservative interior provinces.

Agencia Presentes (19 Mar 2026) on the national hate-crime observatory record: 227 hate crimes based on sexual orientation or gender identity in Argentina in 2025 - up 62% year on year, a ten-year record, one every 38 hours; perpetrators were mostly security-force personnel and unknown assailants in public space, beatings the main modality, institutional violence up from 17 cases (2024) to 64 (2025), 32% of 2025 incidents in police stations or prisons, and 43% of perpetrators strangers to their victims. This province sits under that national picture with no local reporting infrastructure to generate separate records.

Agencia Presentes (19 Mar 2026) on the national hate-crime observatory: 227 hate crimes against LGBT+ people in Argentina in 2025 (up 62%, one every 38 hours), 64 security-force institutional-violence cases vs 17 in 2024, 32% of incidents in stations/prisons, 43% of perpetrators unknown to victims. Directly relevant to this province: between 18 and 26 November 2025 police of Salta, Córdoba and Buenos Aires provinces intervened in the deaths of three LGBT+ people in eight days - this province's forces explicitly named in that documented pattern.

Agencia Presentes (6 Feb 2025): Emergency Decree 62/2025 amends the national Gender Identity Law (26.743) to bar under-18s from gender-affirming surgeries and comprehensive hormonal treatment; Decree 61/2025 changes placement of trans people in the prison system. Both bind every province including this one; FALGBT announced legal action and constitutional experts call the decrees unlawful.
